hits.preview: Hi All Please see below and attached feedback on actions from yesterday’s meeting. Regulatory Confirmation * The angle sensor requirement applies in Europe and Israel but is not mandatory for the UK, avoiding unnecessary procurement for UK vehicles. I checked with Stuart and although the angle sensor is not a requirement for the UK market, we are going to have the angle sensors on F-Series as standard for the UK market. So we will have to work these into the recommended parts list for P700. Digital Process Improvements * Proposal from ITUK to develop an online portal for tracking technical and parts queries submitted to IML, replacing the current email-based process. * The concept will be proposed to Japan and evaluated together with IT to improve transparency and response times. ISZE presented the development of a portal system at the 2024 EU Aftersales conference (refer attached and screenshot below). Has there been any progress on this portal since it was presented in 2024? * Engine & Cab Parts Please see attached “VIN List 23_07_2026”. Is it possible for our colleagues at IML to populate the complete engine, cab with electrics and cab without electrics part numbers and send back to us? This would reduce the amount of time required to quote for cabs and engines in the future. James is going to send the forecast information for dealer sales tomorrow. Kind regards ​​​​​ Duncan

hits.subject: RE: Situation Iran / Impact on purchases & sales
hits.preview: Hi Jerome I've responded to each of your questions below on my view of the UK market across both vehicles and parts. 1. Customer sentiment vs. 6 months ago Sentiment has noticeably softened. Six months ago we were seeing reasonably steady enquiry levels on the vehicle side and customers were broadly willing to commit to orders within their planning cycles. Today, conversations are taking longer, decisions are being deferred, and customers are asking more questions around total cost of ownership, residuals and lead times before they commit. The current geopolitical situation is part of it, but it's compounding pressures that were already there, interest rates, cost of living increases, and uncertainty around the broader UK economic and political outlook. Seems we again might have a Prime Minister change on the horizon if I listen to the news this weekend and that has historically not been good for customer confidence. On the parts side, the picture is somewhat different. Operators are keeping vehicles in service longer, which is supporting aftersales demand, but customers are increasingly price-sensitive and we're seeing more scrutiny on parts pricing, more requests for quotes against alternatives, and pressure on the dealer network to remain competitive against independent factors \ aftermarket suppliers. 2. hits.subject: RE: NOX Sensor SPA
hits.preview: Hi Jerome, To address your points. 1. Expand the parts scope Please add 20–30 parts to the SPA proposal — specifically lines where you see a realistic opportunity to grow sales significantly. The goal is twofold: a broader proposal has a better chance of internal approval, and it helps offset the lost turnover from brake parts with lines where we can genuinely increase volume. Low-hanging fruit preferred but I guess that will be hard anyway. I was under the impression this was a credit based SPA. Thus the objective is not only to grow sales but the recoup the stock value written off. Thus parts should be irrelevant, but more exercise in how we would like our money back. 2. Cost split with JP To support internal approval on our side, I'd like to push for JP to carry the bulk of the ISZE/IML cost share. The basis for that is straightforward — they still have an open repayment on the NOx sensor, which gives us a reasonable argument to position their contribution as part of that settlement rather than a new ask. Let me know if you need any clarification on either point. hits.preview: Good morning Koen, thank you for reaching out and for sharing your observation. The recent decline in order intake and sales is indeed partly linked to the Iran situation and the resulting market uncertainties. Over the past six months—and particularly in March—we proactively increased our stock levels for selected product groups to mitigate potential supply risks and ensure continuity. As a result, some of our customers and internal demand have been covered through these previously built-up inventories, which is currently reducing the need for new orders At this stage, we do not see a structural issue, but rather a temporary normalization following the earlier stock build-up combined with the external geopolitical situation. We appreciate your support and will of course keep you updated should the situation change or if specific actions are required. Please let me know if you would like to discuss this in more detail. hits.preview: Dear Koen, please find below my feedback: 1. Customer sentiment in our market has slightly weakened compared to 6 months ago. Customers are generally more cautious and tend to delay purchasing decisions. 2. Rising fuel prices have had a noticeable impact on customer behavior. There is increased price sensitivity and closer scrutiny of total cost of ownership. Additionally, customers are driving less due to higher fuel costs, which leads to extended service intervals. However, we do not see a significant decline in customer visits to the dealer network at this stage. 3. For the next 3–6 months, we expect demand to remain stable at a slightly lower level, with ongoing uncertainty influencing buying decisions. No strong recovery is anticipated in the short term. hits.subject: AW: Business impact of the Iran conflict
hits.preview: Dear Ling, thank you for reaching out and for the opportunity to share our assessment regarding the potential business impact arising from the ongoing conflict involving Iran. Based on our current observations, we would like to summarize our views as follows: Financial Impact We anticipate increased transportation and logistics costs, primarily driven by rising fuel prices and higher risk premiums in international transport. Depending on further developments, we estimate an increase in transport-related costs in the high single‑digit to low double‑digit percentage range. At the same time, weakened demand on the vehicle market may exert pressure on revenues. Qualitative Impact Beyond the direct financial effects, we observe a growing level of uncertainty among customers. The geopolitical situation is contributing to a generally more cautious purchasing behavior, particularly for higher-value investments such as vehicles. This is likely to result in delayed purchase decisions and longer sales cycles. Macroeconomic Impact The conflict is expected to further dampen overall economic sentiment. Higher energy and fuel costs reduce consumers’ disposable income and may contribute to slowing economic growth. These are contractual service commitments. For a new model variant like the P700 VK05, where failure patterns are not yet established and model-specific components such as air conditioning are new to the range, parts unavailability would put ITUK directly in breach of those fleet contracts. A robust initial stocking recommendation from IML would help ITUK protect those commitments from day one. Thank you in advance for your support. Please let me know if you need any additional information from our side. Kind regards, Jérôme Van der Pluym Assistant Manager // Pricing analyst Sales – Vehicle Parts | Isuzu Motors Europe NV +3

hits.subject: RE: Minutes ITUK
hits.preview: Hi, Jérôme, Apologies for taking time to get back to you on this one. Can you please elaborate? You make an assumption of ITUK’s purchase to ISZE based on ITUK’s sales to dealers, and set a target amount? Masumi From: Jerome Van Der Pluym <jerome.van.der.pluym@isuzu-e.com> Sent: 17 December 2025 10:56 To: Masumi Hayakawa <masumi.hayakawa@isuzu-e.com> Cc: Sales <sales@isuzu-e.com>; Hadewijch Tibos <hadewijch.tibos@isuzu-e.com>; Bart Symons <bart.symons@isuzu-e.com> Subject: RE: Minutes ITUK Dear Masumi, I asked ITUK’s sales to dealer data as that was the I wanted to work to make the figure less abstract not prone to * inventory changes from the DB. * One-off purchasing behavior linked to campaigns ( or a scrap order for example) Afterwards you mentioned that I needed to work with our sales to DB data, which we did and for which ITUK was not very fond of that idea. Now we need to switch again to sales to dealer data. For Duncan was the issue GEO GDPR related, He wanted to see which dealer area’s were performing well, which we don’t need to do. I can aggregate all their sales data from the file attached and work with these figures, so we don’t need to bother them again. For the rest I have their car park data but it’s until 2024 So I will calculate their genuine parts share for 2024 and set a target for 2025. Kind regards, Jérôme Van der Pluym Assistant Manager // Pricing analyst

It also benefits your own business by providing a clear view of your key performance figures and helping you track your development over time. We sincerely appreciate your ongoing effort and commitment in providing these reports each month. Please make sure to send your file to sales@isuzu-e.com as well as to us. Kind regards, Koen Matheussen Assistant Manager Sales – Vehicle Parts| Isuzu Motors Europe NV +32 471 613 772 Koen.matheussen@isuzu-e.com Bist 12, 2630 Aartselaar, Belgium From: Sebastian Müller <Sebastian.Muller@astara.com> Sent: Wednesday, 3 June 2026 07:29 To: Koen Matheussen <koen.matheussen@isuzu-e.com> Cc: Sales <sales@isuzu-e.com> Subject: AW: Situation Iran / Impact on purchases & sales Good morning Koen, thank you for reaching out and for sharing your observation. The recent decline in order intake and sales is indeed partly linked to the Iran situation and the resulting market uncertainties. Over the past six months—and particularly in March—we proactively increased our stock levels for selected product groups to mitigate potential supply risks and ensure continuity. As a result, some of our customers and internal demand have been covered through these previously built-up inventories, which is currently reducing the need for new orders At this stage, we do not see a structural issue, but rather a temporary normalization following the earlier stock build-up combined with the external geopolitical situation. We appreciate your support and will of course keep you updated

(refer attached e-mail from January 2025) On the earlier vehicle, Japan advised that the correct TCM was PN 8984869510, superseded to 8984869511, and that the unit received was the wrong control unit. At that point ISZE were checking whether this was a mixed/wrong batch issue, and CRs were agreed for the affected units. This current case appears to be the same issue again. The dealer has ordered the correct EPC part number, but the units received are again not programming and are causing multiple DTCs. The vehicle is still VOR and the customer situation is becoming critical. Could you please ask IMG/IML to urgently confirm: * The exact correct TCM part number/configuration required for VIN JAANLR87EJ7100695 * Whether current ISZE/IML stock has been physically checked before shipment * Whether the 3 units being arranged by air can be verified as correct before dispatch * The proposed action for the two failed units already supplied We need a confirmed solution now rather than further trial shipments, as sending more units without verification may not resolve the VOR. Kind Regards ​​​​ Duncan Young Parts Director Isuzu Truck (UK) Ltd Isuzu House, 164 Great North Road Hatfield , Hertfords

hits.subject: RE: Situation Iran / Impact on purchases & sales
hits.preview: Hi Jerome I've responded to each of your questions below on my view of the UK market across both vehicles and parts. 1. Customer sentiment vs. 6 months ago Sentiment has noticeably softened. Six months ago we were seeing reasonably steady enquiry levels on the vehicle side and customers were broadly willing to commit to orders within their planning cycles. Today, conversations are taking longer, decisions are being deferred, and customers are asking more questions around total cost of ownership, residuals and lead times before they commit. The current geopolitical situation is part of it, but it's compounding pressures that were already there, interest rates, cost of living increases, and uncertainty around the broader UK economic and political outlook. Seems we again might have a Prime Minister change on the horizon if I listen to the news this weekend and that has historically not been good for customer confidence. On the parts side, the picture is somewhat different. Operators are keeping vehicles in service longer, which is supporting aftersales demand, but customers are increasingly price-sensitive and we're seeing more scrutiny on parts pricing, more requests for quotes against alternatives, and pressure on the dealer network to remain competitive against independent factors \ aftermarket suppliers. 2. I fully understand that the minutes were produced in good faith following a very busy and detailed trip. The reason for the detailed feedback was simply because the document had already been circulated to senior management, and it is important that any inaccuracies, missing context, or UK market misunderstandings are corrected before the report is relied upon more broadly for future decisions. A number of the discussions during the visits were quite detailed and specific to the UK market, particularly around servicing intervals, TCO, dealer retention, and aftermarket competition, so I want to ensure the final document properly reflects the context behind those conversations and does not unintentionally create an incorrect impression of the UK market position or ITUK operations. hits.subject: Parts Month End Report - April 2026
hits.preview: Hi Pete Please see attached report of parts performance for April 2026. Headlines below April delivered a strong start to the new fiscal year, with parts sales of £1.17m outperforming plan by c.16% (£1.01m), driven by effective clutch and service promotions and increased dealer activity. Daily run rate is up 14.5% year-on-year, while stock has been proactively reduced following prior buy-forward activity, with MOS improving slightly to 4.5. First pick rate dipped to 94.5% due to temporary ISZE/IML portal issues (now resolved), which should support recovery in May. hits.subject: RE: Questions
hits.preview: Hi Jerome From an ITUK perspective, the rationale for ISZE’s €10,000 contribution is not based on a direct or immediate financial return from the UK market alone, but rather on supporting a strategic initiative that strengthens genuine parts sales and retention for both ITUK and ultimately also ISZE. The platform is designed to address future parts sales opportunities, for example targeting 3rd party repairers to claw back business currently going to factor parts suppliers like CV Components. A significant proportion of lost sales to the aftermarket is driven not by price, but by convenience and availability. By improving the ordering experience we expect to: * Increase order frequency from existing dealer and fleet customers * Improve retention of genuine parts by reducing leakage to factors * Provide a route to market for independent repairers who are currently outside of the network In terms of financial return, while it is difficult to attribute a precise figure at this early stage, our expectation is that a relatively small uplift in parts sales will cover the €10,000 investment within a short period. For context, an increase of approximately 1–2% in annual parts turnover would be sufficient to offset this cost. If ITUK parts sales increase, so will ISZE parts sales increase. We will closely monitor performance post-implementation and will be able to provide more concrete

hits.subject: RE: Questions
hits.preview: Hi Jerome Yes, your understanding is broadly correct. We are currently implementing a digital parts ordering platform in partnership with Adventoris. The scope includes a mobile ordering app, web-based ordering, a B2C module, and push notification capability. The primary objective is to increase parts sales and provide us a tool to go to market and target 3rd party repairers that might be using factor parts suppliers that we can convert to Isuzu genuine parts. We expect to improve market share of genuine Isuzu parts, enhance customer engagement, and minimise the risk of customers turning to the aftermarket due to convenience factors. hits.subject: RE: Cab Issue Lead time
hits.preview: Hi Jerome, This situation is extremely concerning from a customer and market perspective. Delays of this magnitude simply do not occur with other manufacturers in the UK when ordering a replacement cab. If the lead time is likely to extend to eight months or more before the cab can even be supplied, most insurance companies will simply write the vehicle off rather than wait for the repair to be completed. The longer-term risk for us is that once a vehicle is written off, the customer often replaces it with another brand. Situations like this therefore have a direct impact not only on parts sales but also on future vehicle sales and overall brand confidence in the market. Additionally, once the vehicle is written off it goes to a breaker-yard and the second-hand parts are sold into the market, so we actually lose two potential sales of parts for every vehicle that is written off. * What happened to the idea of ISZE keeping a few cabs in stock? * @James Marsh <mailto:james.marsh@isuzutruck.co.uk> what does our stock of cabs currently look like in the UK? * @Jerome Van Der Pluym <mailto:jerome.van.der.pluym@isuzu-e.com> has there been any progress on the cab vin\part number project? We urgently need clarity on whether there is any way to accelerate the creation of the part number and subsequent supply of the cab. atts: Budget Intial Figures FY26 FY27 FY28.xlsx
hits.preview: Hi Hadi As discussed earlier today, please find attached the proposed plan for FY26, 27, 28, taking into account the R51 issue. My comments * As of today, my FY25 forecast closing figure stands at £12,366,456. This remains ahead of our original planning assumption of £12,250,000 set at the beginning of the year. The subsequent increase to £12,690,000 was introduced under pressure and will be challenging to deliver by the close of FY26. We will of course keep pushing to achieve this number. * Based on the current forecast position, my proposed FY26 target of £12,987,500 represents an increase of approximately 5%. This is a realistic reflection of current UK market conditions, particularly considering the continued negative year-on-year performance, based on the latest registration statistics I showed you earlier. * We already know that the P700 SOP will slip by at least one month, moving from April to May, with a strong possibility of further delay. * Due to our current model not meeting the R51 drive-by noise regulation, it is likely we will be without N35 stock for an extended period. As this model is primarily retail-focused, customers are unlikely to wait for availability and will instead purchase competitor products, which long term is not good for parts sales. ​​​​ Duncan Young Head of Parts Isuzu Truck (UK) Ltd Isuzu House, 164 Great North Road Hatfield , Hertfordshire ,

hits.subject: RE: NOX Sensor SPA
hits.preview: Hi Jerome, To address your points. 1. Expand the parts scope Please add 20–30 parts to the SPA proposal — specifically lines where you see a realistic opportunity to grow sales significantly. The goal is twofold: a broader proposal has a better chance of internal approval, and it helps offset the lost turnover from brake parts with lines where we can genuinely increase volume. Low-hanging fruit preferred but I guess that will be hard anyway. I was under the impression this was a credit based SPA. Thus the objective is not only to grow sales but the recoup the stock value written off. Thus parts should be irrelevant, but more exercise in how we would like our money back. 2. Cost split with JP To support internal approval on our side, I'd like to push for JP to carry the bulk of the ISZE/IML cost share. The basis for that is straightforward — they still have an open repayment on the NOx sensor, which gives us a reasonable argument to position their contribution as part of that settlement rather than a new ask. Let me know if you need any clarification on either point. hits.preview: Dear Suzuki san, Thank you for your time this week it was a pleasure to meet with you and thank you for the wrap up document. To be successful, I think we should focus on the newer models which are the N35.125 and N35.150 which have the RZ4E and 4JZ1 engines respectively. Based on this, please refer to the owner’s manual that reflects the NLR87 which is the RZ4E engine and has a maintenance interval of 20,000kms and the NLR88 which has a flexible maintenance interval up to 40,000kms. Also, these are all 3.5t vehicles which we know are difficult to locate and my understanding was that we would look at targeting 7.5t customers primarily fleet customers where we see the greatest potential opportunity whereby both engine types 4JZ1 and 4HK1 NPR88 and NPR75 respectively both have a maintenance interval of 40,000kms. If you need some further support with the maintenance intervals and model types, please let me know. I will also as agreed look at our average brake pad replacement cycle based on 7.5t for vehicles on R&M and let you know. Kind Regards Tim Tim Hicks​​​​ Operations & Product Director Isuzu Truck (UK) Ltd Isuzu House, 164 Great North Road Hatfield

hits.subject: Re: IDS evaluation sheet + I. VIS manual
hits.preview: Dear Onozato-san, Thank you for your email. I would like to clarify that my concern is not related to how ITUK may be perceived. Rather, my primary concern is the scope of the standards included in the evaluation. As mentioned at the outset, ITUK has a number of additional standards that are essential to our business operations. At this stage, it is not possible for us to exclude these items. If we were to distribute an evaluation sheet that does not reflect the full set of requirements, there is a risk that Dealers may assume these additional items are no longer mandatory. One specific example is the set of standards related to our UK specific Customer CARE programme. These requirements are critical to our operation, and we must ensure that Dealers formally commit to them. Conducting a standards assessment without including these items would prevent us from effectively enforcing compliance and could create significant operational issues. For our business to function successfully, all required standards must be clearly communicated and fully complied with. We cannot proceed with an approach that may lead Dealers to believe partial compliance is acceptable. With the greatest respect, this is not something ITUK is able to proceed with. Kind regards, Tim Tim Hicks​​​​ Head of Operations & Product Isuzu Truck (UK) Ltd Isuzu House, 164 Great North Road Hatfield , Hertfordshire , AL9

hits.subject: Re: IDS evaluation sheet + I. VIS manual
hits.preview: Dear Koen, Thank you very much for the information and related documents. This is a difficult situation for ITUK to perform, for two reasons as I explained previously to Onozato san. For the UK market, we use the standard evaluation criteria, however, we also include quite a large number of additional Dealer Standards for our Network over and above the standard ones. Also, we do not have weighting when we score the Dealer, we only have pass or fail, because if you have a standard, then it is a standard as far as we are concerned and you cannot partly comply. We also produce a detailed document that explains each standard for the dealer and what it means for them to fully understand. We wouldn’t assess our Dealers in the way you have indicated and I did explain this to Onozato san, as this would actually reduce the current standards we assess and we cannot do that. We will assess the Dealers based on our current standards and supply this information, but we cannot apply standards that are lower than our current one. hits.preview: Dear Koen, thank you for sharing your estimates and background on the methodology. We have reviewed the active parc figures for Germany based on our available data (source: Management Services Helwig Schmitt GmbH, vehicle parc overview as of 31/12/2025). Please find our figures below: Active Parc Germany (as of 31/12/2025) * Total Isuzu Parc: 13,835 units Breakdown: * D-Max / Pick-Up (incl. Off-Road & related segments): approx. 13,048 units * N-Series (Light & Medium Duty Trucks): approx. 787 units This results in a total actively operating parc that is slightly higher than your estimate (12,855 units). N-Series Breakdown (by tonnage) * ≤ 3.5t: 153 units * 3.51 – 5.5t: 79 units * 5.51 – 6.5t: 147 units * 6.51 – 7.5t: 318 units * 7.51 – 12.0t: 35 units Source of Data The figures are based on external market data (Management Services Helwig Schmitt GmbH), reflecting the active registered vehicle parc. Remarks on Deviations The higher total compared to your model may be driven by: * Longer vehicle lifetime in the German market * Continued operation of older vehicles, especially in the light truck segment * Differences between registration-based parc data and shipment/survival curve methodology At this stage, we do not apply a separate internal scrap or deregistration rate. ________________________________ Please let us know if you need any further breakdown or clarification. hits.subject: AW: Situation Iran / Impact on purchases & sales
hits.preview: Good morning Koen, thank you for reaching out and for sharing your observation. The recent decline in order intake and sales is indeed partly linked to the Iran situation and the resulting market uncertainties. Over the past six months—and particularly in March—we proactively increased our stock levels for selected product groups to mitigate potential supply risks and ensure continuity. As a result, some of our customers and internal demand have been covered through these previously built-up inventories, which is currently reducing the need for new orders At this stage, we do not see a structural issue, but rather a temporary normalization following the earlier stock build-up combined with the external geopolitical situation. We appreciate your support and will of course keep you updated should the situation change or if specific actions are required. Please let me know if you would like to discuss this in more detail. Best regards, Sebastian Mit freundlichen Grüßen / Best regards Sebastian Müller Head of Aftersales ISUZU Sales Deutschland GmbH Schieferstein 11A | 65439 Flörsheim am Main s.mueller@isuzu-sales.de <mailto:s.mueller@isuzu-sales.de> T: +49 6145 549 1130 | M: +49 172 8611060 ISUZU <https://cas5-0-urlprotect.trendmicro.com:443/wis/clicktime/v1/query?url=https%3a%2f%2fwww.isuzu%2dsales.de&umid=33ab2b2b-5f0d-11f1-90f4-7ced8dbe8bea&rct=1780464576&auth=c409b3fe49adaa4cc1

Customers are generally more cautious and tend to delay purchasing decisions. 2. Rising fuel prices have had a noticeable impact on customer behavior. There is increased price sensitivity and closer scrutiny of total cost of ownership. Additionally, customers are driving less due to higher fuel costs, which leads to extended service intervals. However, we do not see a significant decline in customer visits to the dealer network at this stage. 3. For the next 3–6 months, we expect demand to remain stable at a slightly lower level, with ongoing uncertainty influencing buying decisions. No strong recovery is anticipated in the short term. Please let me know if further details are required. hits.subject: AW: Business impact of the Iran conflict
hits.preview: Dear Ling, thank you for reaching out and for the opportunity to share our assessment regarding the potential business impact arising from the ongoing conflict involving Iran. Based on our current observations, we would like to summarize our views as follows: Financial Impact We anticipate increased transportation and logistics costs, primarily driven by rising fuel prices and higher risk premiums in international transport. Depending on further developments, we estimate an increase in transport-related costs in the high single‑digit to low double‑digit percentage range. At the same time, weakened demand on the vehicle market may exert pressure on revenues. Qualitative Impact Beyond the direct financial effects, we observe a growing level of uncertainty among customers. The geopolitical situation is contributing to a generally more cautious purchasing behavior, particularly for higher-value investments such as vehicles. This is likely to result in delayed purchase decisions and longer sales cycles. Macroeconomic Impact The conflict is expected to further dampen overall economic sentiment. Higher energy and fuel costs reduce consumers’ disposable income and may contribute to slowing economic growth. hits.subject: Recommended parts list ITUK
hits.preview: Hello Suzuki san, I hope you are well. Following your visit to ITUK for the PMS program introduction, I wanted to share a related request that has come in from their side. ITUK has contacted us asking for a recommended initial stocking parts list for the new P700 VK05 model. This is a new configuration for the UK market, introducing components not previously fitted to earlier models — notably air conditioning — and ITUK wants to be well prepared ahead of the launch. The commercial urgency behind this request is ITUK's I-Maintain Repair & Maintenance contract program, under which fleet customers pay a fixed monthly fee covering all scheduled servicing, safety inspections, repairs, and MOT preparation — carried out exclusively through the Isuzu dealer network. These are contractual service commitments. For a new model variant like the P700 VK05, where failure patterns are not yet established and model-specific components such as air conditioning are new to the range, parts unavailability would put ITUK directly in breach of those fleet contracts. A robust initial stocking recommendation from IML would help ITUK protect those commitments from day one. Thank you in advance for your support. Please let me know if you need any additional information from our side. Kind regards, Jérôme Van der Pluym Assistant Manager // Pricing analyst Sales – Vehicle Parts | Isuzu Motors Europe NV +3

Now we need to switch again to sales to dealer data. For Duncan was the issue GEO GDPR related, He wanted to see which dealer area’s were performing well, which we don’t need to do. I can aggregate all their sales data from the file attached and work with these figures, so we don’t need to bother them again. For the rest I have their car park data but it’s until 2024 So I will calculate their genuine parts share for 2024 and set a target for 2025. hits.subject: Recommended parts list ITUK
hits.preview: Hello Suzuki san, I hope you are well. Following your visit to ITUK for the PMS program introduction, I wanted to share a related request that has come in from their side. ITUK has contacted us asking for a recommended initial stocking parts list for the new P700 VK05 model. This is a new configuration for the UK market, introducing components not previously fitted to earlier models — notably air conditioning — and ITUK wants to be well prepared ahead of the launch. The commercial urgency behind this request is ITUK's I-Maintain Repair & Maintenance contract program, under which fleet customers pay a fixed monthly fee covering all scheduled servicing, safety inspections, repairs, and MOT preparation — carried out exclusively through the Isuzu dealer network. These are contractual service commitments. For a new model variant like the P700 VK05, where failure patterns are not yet established and model-specific components such as air conditioning are new to the range, parts unavailability would put ITUK directly in breach of those fleet contracts. A robust initial stocking recommendation from IML would help ITUK protect those commitments from day one. Thank you in advance for your support. Please let me know if you need any additional information from our side. Kind regards, Jérôme Van der Pluym Assistant Manager // Pricing analyst Sales – Vehicle Parts | Isuzu Motors Europe NV +3

hits.preview: Dear Yoshimoto san, ITUK operates in a competitive UK parts market where dealers regularly face pressure from aftermarket suppliers and second-hand parts. When the price gap is too wide, dealers lose the sale — and once a customer moves to aftermarket, they are very hard to recover. DLOD is a structured price support mechanism that allows ITUK to offer competitive pricing on a case-by-case basis, retaining customers on genuine Isuzu parts. From ISZE's perspective, this is a direct revenue protection measure. Every part ITUK retains is a unit we sell upstream. The €30,000 annual envelope is a fixed, controlled commitment to defend a revenue stream worth significantly more across the active UK parc. ITUK provides full deal activity records as evidence, giving us visibility into where genuine parts are price-uncompetitive in the market. hits.subject: Target ITUK
hits.preview: Dear Duncan, Dear James, We have received your latest SOR orders and noted a total value of approximately €67k. Based on our current tracking, this brings ITUK’s invoiced purchases to around €4.39m, compared to a full-year plan (including January) of €4.89m. This implies a remaining gap of roughly €0.5m with a good two months left in the period. As PRD orders placed at this stage will not be invoiced within the current financial year, any catch-up would therefore need to come from SOR volumes. We have also observed that ITUK’s purchasing activity has slowed somewhat since December. It would be helpful to understand whether the current plan is still considered achievable from your side, or if expectations have changed. ( Below is ITUK’s purchases until yesterday) The reason we are reaching out at this point is that our management is currently very closely monitoring KOSHA and overall plan adherence. Given ITUK’s importance within our network, any deviation versus plan understandably has a disproportionate impact at group level, which makes early visibility especially important for us. Please let us know your view and of course feel free to reach out if you would like to discuss this in more detail.
